CORE.doc:
Core, rhc's typed lazy intermediate language (the haskell98 roadmap, D2):
System F with type constructors applied to types (`m a`), a lazy `let`
and `letrec`, and a `case` that is the only thing that forces. A value
is passed by an atom, a variable or a literal, so every allocation is a
`let` and every evaluation a `case`.

A type says whether a value may be unevaluated. A binding of a lifted
type `T` may hold a suspension; one of `!T` holds a value evaluated to
weak head normal form. `!` stands only where a value is bound: at a
lambda's binder, a function's parameter, a constructor's field and a
component of an unboxed tuple, and the binder of a `case` and the
fields it binds are of the evaluated type. So a strictness result has
a type to go to, and Core to Mid knows which positions are `susp T` and
which `T`. Where an evaluated value meets a lazy position, `!T` is taken
for `T`; the other way is a `case`.

An unlifted type, the state token `World` and an unboxed tuple, is
never suspended: no `let` binds it, and a `case` takes it apart. `IO a`
is `World -> (utuple World a)` in the Prelude's Core (D25).

members.name: kind
members.spec:
datatype kind =
    Star
  | Unlifted
  | Arrow of kind * kind
members.doc: The kind of a type.

members.name: ty
members.spec:
datatype ty =
    TVar of string
  | TCon of string
  | TApp of ty * ty
  | TFun of ty * ty
  | TForall of string * kind * ty
  | TEval of ty
  | TUTuple of ty list
members.doc: A type.

members.name: lit
members.spec:
datatype lit =
    LInt of IntInf.int
  | LInteger of IntInf.int
  | LChar of int
  | LDouble of string
  | LFloat of string
  | LStr of string
members.doc: A literal. A floating literal keeps the digits it was written with.

members.name: atom
members.spec: datatype atom = Var of string | Lit of lit
members.doc: An argument: a variable or a literal.

members.name: arg
members.spec: datatype arg = TyArg of ty | ValArg of atom
members.doc: What an application gives a function.

members.name: binder
members.spec: datatype binder = TyBinder of string * kind | ValBinder of string * ty
members.doc: What a lambda binds.

members.name: exp
members.spec:
datatype exp =
    Atom of atom
  | App of exp * arg list
  | Lam of binder list * exp
  | Let of string * ty * exp * exp
  | LetRec of (string * ty * exp) list * exp
  | Case of exp * string * alt list
  | Con of string * ty list * atom list
  | Prim of string * ty list * atom list
  | UTuple of atom list
  | Cast of exp * ty
members.doc: An expression. A binder named `_` binds nothing.

members.name: alt
members.spec:
datatype alt =
    AltCon of string * string list * exp
  | AltLit of lit * exp
  | AltUTuple of string list * exp
  | AltDefault of exp
members.doc: An alternative of a `case`.

members.name: decl
members.spec:
datatype decl =
    Data of string * (string * kind) list * (string * ty list) list
  | Newtype of string * (string * kind) list * string * ty
  | Val of string * ty * exp
  | Import of string * ty
members.doc:
A declaration of a program. Every value of the top level is in the
scope of all of them.

members.name: program
members.doc:
A program: what it declares, in order. `main`, of type
`World -> (utuple World T)`, is what runs.

members.name: builtinTypes
members.doc:
`builtinTypes` is each type constructor built in with its kind: `Int`,
`Integer`, `Char`, `Double`, `Float`, `Str`, `Exn`, `Bool`, `World`,
`Ref`, `Arr` and `->`.

`->` is the function type's constructor, which a type holds given
fewer than two arguments (Haskell's `(->)` in an instance's head, 4.3.2);
given both it is the function type, `TFun`, which `apply` and
`substTy` make it.

members.name: builtinData
members.doc:
`builtinData` is the data types built in: `Bool`, whose constructors
`False` and `True` are 0 and 1, as Mid's `bool`.

members.name: stripEval
members.doc: `stripEval t` is `t` without a `!` at its head.

members.name: isEval
members.doc: `isEval t` is whether `t` has a `!` at its head.

members.name: spine
members.spec: val spine : ty -> ty * ty list
members.doc: `spine t` is the head of the type application `t` and its arguments.

members.name: apply
members.spec: val apply : ty * ty list -> ty
members.doc: `apply (t, args)` applies `t` to `args`, left to right.

members.name: freeTyVars
members.doc: `freeTyVars t` is the type variables free in `t`, each once.

members.name: substTy
members.spec: val substTy : (string * ty) list * ty -> ty
members.doc:
`substTy (s, t)` replaces each variable of `s` free in `t` by its type,
renaming a binder of `t` that would capture a variable of those types.

members.name: equalTy
members.doc:
`equalTy (a, b)` is whether `a` and `b` are the same type, up to the
names of their bound variables.

members.name: litTy
members.doc: `litTy l` is the type of the literal `l`, without `!`.

members.name: lamTy
members.spec: val lamTy : binder list * ty -> ty
members.doc:
`lamTy (binders, t)` is the type of a lambda of `binders` whose body
has type `t`.

CORE_GEN.doc:
A generator of Core programs (the haskell98 roadmap, D55, its second
generator): well-typed lazy programs in Pałka's shape, a function from a
list of `Int` to another, made of `map`, `take`, `let`, `letrec`, `case`
and forcing, applied to a partial list, one with a bottom for an element
or its tail, and its result printed to twenty elements.

A program it makes passes CoreLint and runs to an outcome, a value or a
bottom, so that the text, the check, the interpreter and, later, the VM
can be held to each other on what nobody wrote by hand.

members.name: program
members.doc: `program seed` is the program of `seed`: the same for the same seed.

CORE_INTERP.doc:
The Core interpreter (the haskell98 roadmap, M8): Launchbury's natural
semantics of laziness as the specification, and Sestoft's machine as
the program, slow by design. A `let` puts a suspension in the heap; a
variable forced is evaluated once, under a marker that blackholes it,
and updated with its value; a `case` waits on the stack for its
scrutinee. Types are erased.

It is rhc's nearest reference: what the VM prints of a Core program, the
interpreter must print too. An exception that passes a suspension under
evaluation puts the suspension back, so that it raises again when it is
forced again; a suspension forced under its own evaluation raises
`NonTermination`. The stack lives in the heap, so a deep recursion is a
bound of the interpreter's and not the host's.

members.name: outcome
members.spec:
datatype outcome =
    Exit of int
  | Raised of string * string
  | TooDeep
  | OutOfSteps
members.doc:
How a run ended. Every outcome but `Exit 0` is a failure, and a
raise, a stack too deep and steps run out are one bottom.

members.name: Stuck
members.doc:
The interpreter met Core no rule of CoreLint allows: a variable not
bound, a suspension given to a strict parameter, a value no
alternative matches.

members.name: run
members.spec:
val run : {program : Core.program, steps : int option, depth : int, out : string -> unit, err : string -> unit}
          -> {outcome : outcome, steps : int}
members.doc:
`run {program, steps, depth, out, err}` runs `main` of `program`, a
program CoreLint passed, and says how the run ended and the steps it
took.

What it prints to standard output goes to `out`, and to standard error
to `err`. At most `steps` steps are taken where it is `SOME`, and the
stack is at most `depth` deep.

**Raises** `Stuck` where `program` breaks a rule of Core, and where it has
no `main`.

CORE_LINT.doc:
CoreLint (the haskell98 roadmap, D2, D54): the check of a Core program.
Core is explicitly typed, so the check is syntax-directed and unifies
nothing: it works out the type of every expression from its parts and
holds each to what its place wants. rhc runs it on Core read as text,
at each boundary, and last before the crossing into Mid, where `Any`
leaves MidLint weaker; a forgotten force, a lazy atom where `!T` is
wanted, is the breach it is for above all.

Each rule has a name, which its breach's message starts with in
brackets: `[force] in val main: ...`.

members.name: Error
members.doc: A breach of a rule: its message, `[RULE] in val NAME: what is wrong`.

members.name: rules
check
members.doc:
`check program` is `()` where `program` keeps every rule.

**Raises** `Error` at the first breach.

CORE_PRIM.doc:
The primitives of Core (the haskell98 roadmap, D26): what Core can do
that is not a function of Core, each with its type. An argument a
primitive reads is evaluated, `!T`; one it may leave suspended, a
function or a value it stores, is lazy. A primitive that does I/O takes
the state token and gives it back, so that its order is its data's.

They are Rune's primitives where Mid has one of the same name, and do
what it does: `int_add` raises `Overflow` past `Int`'s range, as
`Int.+` does, and a division by zero raises `Div`. Core to Mid lowers
each; the Core interpreter runs each (CoreInterp).

members.name: prim
members.spec: type prim = {name : string, ty : Core.ty, doc : string}
members.doc: A primitive: its name, its type in Core, and what it does.

members.name: prims
members.doc:
`prims` is every primitive, in the order of this list:

- on `Int`: `int_add`, `int_sub`, `int_mul`, `int_quot`, `int_rem`,
  `int_div`, `int_mod`, `int_neg`, and the comparisons `int_eq`,
  `int_ne`, `int_lt`, `int_le`, `int_gt`, `int_ge`;
- on `Integer`: the same, `integer_add` to `integer_ge`, and
  `integer_from_int`, `integer_to_int`;
- on `Char`: `char_ord`, `char_chr`, and `char_eq` to `char_ge`;
- on `Double`: `double_add`, `double_sub`, `double_mul`, `double_div`,
  `double_neg`, `double_eq` to `double_ge`, `double_from_int` and
  `double_to_str`; then the elementary functions `double_sqrt`,
  `double_exp`, `double_log`, `double_sin`, `double_cos`, `double_tan`,
  `double_atan`, `double_sinh`, `double_cosh`, `double_tanh` and
  `double_atan2`; the conversions to `Int` `double_truncate`,
  `double_round` (to even at a half), `double_ceiling`, `double_floor`;
  the classes `double_is_nan`, `double_is_infinite`,
  `double_is_negative_zero`, `double_is_denormalized`;
  `double_decode` and `double_encode`, a mantissa of 53 bits; and
  `double_pow`;
- on `Float`, a `Double` that binary32 represents, every result of
  arithmetic rounded to binary32 by Mid's `real_to_single` (D23):
  `float_add`, `float_sub`, `float_mul`, `float_div`, `float_neg`,
  `float_eq` to `float_ge`, `float_from_int`, `float_from_double`,
  `float_to_double`, `float_to_str`, and the functions of `Double`
  from the elementary ones on, `float_sqrt` to `float_encode`, a
  mantissa of 24 bits;
- on `Str`: `str_size`, `str_byte`, `str_concat`, `str_from_char`,
  `str_extract`, `str_eq`;
- on `Arr a`, an array of cells each holding a value, unforced, as
  `Ref a` does one: `arr_new`, `arr_set`, `arr_read`, `arr_get`,
  `arr_size`;
- I/O: `print_str`, `print_err`, `exit`; the handles of files, 0 to 2
  standard input, output and error, `h_open`, `h_close`, `h_read`,
  `h_write`, `h_flush`, `h_error`; `interleave`, which defers an
  action until its value is forced (D25's one interleaving
  primitive); `ref_new`, `ref_get`, `ref_set`, `real_world`;
- exceptions: `raise`, `raise_io`, `exn_error`, `exn_io`, `exn_io_full`,
  `exn_io_code`, `exn_io_file`, `exn_io_handle`, `exn_pattern`,
  `exn_kind`, `exn_name`, `exn_message` and `catch`;
- then each family's, in the order of `families`.

members.name: find
members.doc: `find name` is the primitive called `name`, if there is one.

members.name: families
members.doc:
`families` is the families of primitives (CORE\_PRIM\_FAMILY), each of a
file of its own.

`prims` lists their primitives after its own: the IO library's
handles and the system's errors (CorePrimIo), and the operating
system's file system, process, clock and randomness, which Directory,
System, Time, CPUTime and Random read (CorePrimSys).

members.name: familyOf
members.doc:
`familyOf name` is the family of the primitive called `name` and the
primitive, where a family has it.

members.name: exnKinds
members.doc:
`exnKinds` is the kinds of exception, by the number `exn_kind` gives.

They are `ErrorCall`, `IOError`, `PatternMatchFail`, `NonTermination`
(a suspension forced again under its own evaluation), `Div`, `Overflow`,
`Subscript`, `Chr` and `Domain` (a NaN made an `Int`).

CORE_PRIM_FAMILY.doc:
A family of Core's primitives, defined in a file of its own (the
haskell98 roadmap, M17, M18): each primitive with its type, what the
Core interpreter does for it, and the Mid function Core to Mid lowers it
to, defined in the family's Mid text. CorePrim lists each family's
primitives after its own, CoreInterp runs them and CoreToMid lowers
them, so that a family is added with no edit of any of the three but a
line of CorePrim's.

A primitive of a family takes arguments of `!Int`, `!Str` and `!Bool`,
and the state token where it is an action, and gives an `Int`, a `Str`
or a `Bool`; an action gives `(utuple World T)` of one, or `World`.

members.name: value
members.spec: datatype value = Int of int | Str of string | Bool of bool | Unit
members.doc: An argument or a result of a primitive of a family.

members.name: IOError
members.spec: exception IOError of int * string * string * int
members.doc:
What a primitive raises in the interpreter where it fails: an
`IOError` of a code, a text, a file and a handle, as `exn_io_full`
makes one.

members.name: prim
members.spec: type prim = {name : string, ty : string, doc : string, run : value list -> value, mid : string}
members.doc:
A primitive: its name, its type, what it does, what the interpreter
does for it, and the Mid function it is lowered to.

Its type is Core's text. The interpreter's `run` is given its arguments,
the state token left out; the Mid function takes them too, or `()`
where it takes none.

members.name: family
members.spec: type family = {name : string, prims : prim list, midText : string}
members.doc:
A family: its name, its primitives, and the Mid text that defines
their functions.

The text is a group of `funs`, which Core to Mid adds once to a program
that names any of the family's primitives.

CORE_RUNTIME.doc:
rhc's runtime, in Core (the haskell98 roadmap, M17; D24 to D26): what
the Report's modules name and never define, written in Core over
CorePrim's primitives, so that the Core interpreter and Core to Mid run
one text and no SML stands below Haskell (D26's A).

It holds the built-in syntax, the unit `()` and the list `[]` with its
constructors `[]` and `:` (ov.prelude.unit, ov.prelude.list), and the
two modules the Report imports and never defines: PreludeBuiltin, whose
primitives are those of share/rhc/haskell98's Prelude and PreludeIO, and
UnicodePrims, Char's. Each `prim*` of the Report is a value of it of the
same name, whose type is the Report's in Core: `String` is `([] Char)`,
`IOError` is `Exn` and `IO a` is `World -> (utuple World a)` (D25's
state token). Beside them it has `primSeq`, `primReturnIO` and
`primBindIO` (ov.prelude.seq, ov.prelude.io) and `primUnpackString`,
which makes a string literal, UTF-8 in a `Str`, its list of characters;
and what the library's PreludeRuntime names beside the Report's:
`double_mantissa` and `double_exponent`, `unsafe_perform_io`,
`primPackString`, `primReady`, and `ref_set`, `arr_set`, `h_close`,
`h_flush` and `exit` as actions giving `()`, which Haskell names as
`IO ()`, over CorePrim's of the same names, whose actions give `World`.

Input and output are UTF-8; a byte that starts no sequence of UTF-8 is
read as the character of its number. `getContents` and `readFile` read
a chunk at a time as their list is read, through `interleave`, the one
interleaving primitive, and end their list at an error of reading
(21.2.2); standard output is written before standard input is read.
`getChar` and `getContents` share standard input's buffer. An IOError
the runtime raises has its kind (`exn_io_full`): a failure of the
system's by the name of its error, its text "what: the system's text"
as the library's, the end of standard input 5.

A program ends with every file it opened written (21's text): the VM's
end flushes every file the program holds, and the interpreter's writes
are unbuffered. An exception no handler takes ends it with status 1 and
a line on standard error, an IOError's text as the library's Show
IOError gives it, a user's as "user error (TEXT)" (7.3, 23).

The general category and the simple case mappings are lib/unicode's
(CodePoint, D21), at its version, in tables written from its data:
`isUpper` is true of every letter that is not lower case (R38).

members.name: strings
members.doc:
How a string literal becomes its list (D24).

`Lazy` makes a cell as the list is read (A, decided); `Whole` makes
every cell at the first force (B, built for the owner's measurement).

members.name: reportNames
members.doc:
`reportNames` is the `prim*` of the Report's modules, each a value of
the runtime.

members.name: program
members.doc:
`program strings` is the whole runtime, its literals made as `strings`
says.

**Raises** `CoreText.Error` where its text does not read, a bug of rhc's.

members.name: link
members.doc:
`link strings p` is `p` after the declarations of the runtime that `p`
reaches, through the names it mentions and through theirs.

A declaration `p` makes of a name of the runtime is `p`'s own, and the
runtime's is left out.

members.name: linkUnit
members.doc:
`linkUnit strings p` is the unit `p` after what it reaches of the
runtime, each value imported (the haskell98 roadmap's M21).

What `link` would add is there, but each value an import of the
runtime's unit, whose program is `program`'s, and each type a copy of
the runtime's declaration; an import of the unit's own is kept.

members.name: mentions
members.doc:
`mentions d` is the names the declaration `d` mentions: types,
constructors and values, each as often as it does.

CORE_TEXT.doc:
Core as text, and back (the haskell98 roadmap, D2): the contract between
the front end, which writes Core, and Core to Mid, which reads it. `show`
prints a program for a dump (rhc --dump-after) or a test (tests/hs/core),
and `parse` reads what it prints, so that print, read, print is the
identity; rhc checks that at lint level 3.

The text is of parenthesised forms. A comment runs from `;` to the end
of its line.

```sml
program := decl ...
decl    := (data T (TYPARAM ...) (C TYPE ...) ...)
         | (newtype T (TYPARAM ...) C TYPE)
         | (val x TYPE EXP)
typaram := a | (a KIND)                  a alone is of kind *
kind    := * | # | (-> KIND KIND ...)    # is unlifted
type    := T | a | (TYPE TYPE ...) | (-> TYPE TYPE ...)
         | (forall (TYPARAM ...) TYPE) | (utuple TYPE ...) | !TYPE
exp     := ATOM | (EXP ARG ...) | (\ (BINDER ...) EXP)
         | (let (x TYPE EXP) EXP) | (letrec ((x TYPE EXP) ...) EXP)
         | (case EXP x ALT ...) | (con C @TYPE ... ATOM ...)
         | (prim P @TYPE ... ATOM ...) | (utuple ATOM ...) | (cast EXP TYPE)
binder  := (x TYPE) | @a | @(a KIND)
arg     := ATOM | @TYPE
alt     := ((C x ...) EXP) | (LITERAL EXP) | ((utuple x ...) EXP) | (_ EXP)
atom    := x | LITERAL
literal := 42 | -42 | 42I | 2.5 | 2.5e-3 | 2.5F | 'c' | '\955' | "bytes"
```

A word in a type is a variable where a `forall`, a type binder or the
parameters of a declaration bind it, and a type constructor elsewhere.
A literal ending in `I` is an `Integer`, one with a point or an exponent
a `Double`, or a `Float` ending in `F`. A string's escapes are `\\`,
`\"`, `\n`, `\t` and `\DDD`, a byte in three decimal digits; a
character's are those, `\'` and `\D...`, a code point in decimal. A name
that is a word of the syntax (`let`, `case`, `*`, `_`, ...), that starts
as a literal, `@` or `!` would, or that holds a space, a parenthesis, a
quotation mark, `;` or a backquote, is written between backquotes, with
`\\` and a backslashed backquote inside.

members.name: Error
members.doc: A fault in the text: the line it is on, and what is wrong.

members.name: parse
members.doc:
`parse text` is the program `text` holds.

**Raises** `Error` where `text` is not a program.

members.name: parseType
members.doc:
`parseType text` is the type `text` holds, whose variables a `forall`
binds.

**Raises** `Error` where `text` is not one type.

members.name: show
members.doc:
`show program` is the text of `program`, which `parse` reads back as
`program`.

members.name: showTy
members.doc: `showTy t` is the text of the type `t`, on one line.

members.name: showKind
members.doc: `showKind k` is the text of the kind `k`.

members.name: showExp
members.doc: `showExp e` is the text of the expression `e`.

members.name: showLit
members.doc: `showLit l` is the text of the literal `l`.

members.name: showName
members.doc:
`showName x` is the name `x` as the text writes it, between backquotes
where it must be.

CORE_TO_MID.doc:
Core to Mid (the haskell98 roadmap, M10): a Core program as a program
of Mid's text, which rhc reads with Mid's own reader and gives to the
passes from Mid on (MidPipeline), its list without expand.

A lazy position of type T is `T susp` in Mid and an evaluated one `T`:
a binder, a parameter, a field and a component of an unboxed tuple of
type `!T` is the value, one of a lifted `T` a suspension. A function
takes each argument in its slot and returns its value evaluated, so a
datatype-typed variable of Mid is evaluated. A `let` of a value -- a
lambda, a constructor, a literal -- binds the value, and of anything else
a suspension, whose code says it is under evaluation first and updates
it with its value last. A `case` forces its scrutinee and tests its tag;
a value given to a lazy slot is cast into it. A `letrec` of values goes
through cells (D6's A), and a value of the top level that is no function
is a suspension in a global, a CAF. The state token is erased (D25): an
action of Core, `World -> (utuple World T)`, is `unit -> T` in Mid, its
order the order of its lets.

An `Integer` is Mid's `IntInf.int`, an immediate within 63 bits and a
sign and a magnitude past them (M31, D20's D), each literal a global made
once. A type variable applied and a forall inside a type are Mid's own
(M28): a lazy field of a forall holds a suspension at every type, the
forall outside it, and a newtype given fewer arguments than its
parameters is a box, as one that reaches itself is.

members.name: fault
members.doc:
A fault made on purpose, for the tests of what catches it.

They are the roadmap's rhc's mutants of Core to Mid: `ThunkInSlot`, a
suspension used where its value is wanted, unforced; `ForceBehindCast`,
a force made a cast from the suspension to its value; `SuspTypeArg`, a
use's first type argument a slot's type, a suspension's.

members.name: checking
members.doc:
Whether Core to Mid holds what it writes to its own rules, which rhc
sets at lint level 2 (M10b).

A use's type argument is a value's type, never one with `susp` at its
head (D4); the rule is Core to Mid's and not MidLint's, since SML uses
its polymorphic functions at `T susp`.

members.name: Breach
members.doc: A breach of Core to Mid's rules, where `checking` holds: what it is.

members.name: Unsupported
members.doc:
A construct Core has and Core to Mid does not lower: what it is, and
where.

members.name: program
members.spec: val program : {fault : fault option} * Core.program -> string
members.doc:
`program ({fault}, p)` is the text of Mid of the Core program `p`,
which CoreLint passed, with the fault made where it is `SOME`.

A suspension is form C's (the roadmap's M9): made by `thunk_make`,
forced by one `thunk_force` node, its code saying `thunk_blackhole`
first and `thunk_self_update` last.

The text's `do` calls `main`, and prints what an exception no handler
takes is, as Core's interpreter does, an IOError's text as the
library's Show IOError gives it, and ends with status 1.

**Raises** `Unsupported` where `p` needs what Mid has not got.

members.name: abi
members.doc:
How a value of the top level is in Mid, an ABI fact of its interface.

A unit that imports it binds it so (H9): a function global, a
suspension in a global (a CAF), or a literal in a global.

members.name: unit
members.doc:
`unit ({fault, imports, makesShared}, p)` is the text of Mid of the
unit `p` (the haskell98 roadmap's M21).

Each import of another unit is bound as `imports` says that unit's
Core to Mid made it, and each newtype of another unit is a box where
`newtypes` says that unit made it one (an ABI fact, H9); its `boxed`
says so of each newtype the unit declares itself. Its `names` is the name in the text of each value of the top level,
the unit's own and its imports, by its Core name; its `abi` how each
of its own is made. An import is declared in the text as a global of
its scheme whose expression is a placeholder, which the client drops
after reading the text, its scheme MidLint's for the import
(MidLint.importedScheme). The text calls `main` where the unit
defines it, as `program`'s does.

**Raises** `Unsupported` where `p` needs what Mid has not got, or an
import `imports` does not give.

members.name: shared
members.doc:
`shared` is the globals of every text's prelude that have an
identity, Core's exceptions, which one unit of a program makes.

Each is in `unit`'s `names` by itself, and
in its `abi` where the unit makes them (makesShared), which one unit
of a program does; in the others' texts they are imports, which their
client reads as it reads an import's placeholder.

CORE_UNITS.doc:
Core in units (the haskell98 roadmap's M21): a program of several units,
each a Core program that names what it takes of the others, a value by
an import (`(import x TYPE)`) and a type by a copy of its declaration,
joined into one program, which Core's interpreter runs and a compile
whole takes.

members.name: Error
members.doc:
what makes units that do not join: a type two units declare apart, or
an import at another type than its definition's

members.name: join
members.doc:
`join units` is the program of the units, in order, each type
declared once and each import given its definition.

A data type or newtype is kept where it is first declared, every unit
that declares it declaring the same; an import is dropped where a unit
defines its value, at the type the import gives it, and kept where
none does.

members.name: unresolved
members.doc:
`unresolved p` is the imports of p that no declaration of p defines,
in order

members.name: uses
members.spec: val uses : Core.decl -> {values : string list, types : string list, cons : string list}
members.doc:
`uses d` is what the declaration `d` names of the top level, each once.

Its values are the variables it names that no binder of it binds; its
types the type constructors it names; its constructors those it makes
or takes apart. A name may be in more than one, as `:` is a value of
the runtime and a constructor of the list.

members.name: reach
members.spec: val reach : Core.program * string list -> Core.program
members.doc:
`reach (p, roots)` is what the values `roots` reach of p, in p's order.

A value reaches the values, types and constructors it names, a
constructor its type, and a type the types of its fields; an import
reached is kept, as a whole program has none (the haskell98 roadmap's
M21: units joined and compiled whole, what main reaches).

members.name: index
members.spec: val index : Core.program -> string * string list
members.doc:
`index p` is the unit `p` as an index and its declarations' texts.

The index says of each declaration, by its number, what it is, its
name, what it makes and what it names, so that `reachIndexed` reads
only the texts of the declarations a program reaches.

members.name: unitCore
members.spec: datatype unitCore = Indexed of string * (int -> string) | InHand of Core.program
members.doc:
A unit's Core as the reach is given it: by its index and a function
from a declaration's number to its text, or in hand.

members.name: reachIndexed
members.spec: val reachIndexed : unitCore list * string list -> Core.program
members.doc:
`reachIndexed (units, roots)` is `reach (join ps, roots)` where `ps` is
the units' programs, a declaration read only where it is reached.

A type is the first unit's that declares it, as `join` keeps it.
Raises `Error` where an index is no index.

members.name: interface
members.spec: val interface : Core.program * string list -> Core.program
members.doc:
`interface (p, exports)` is what a client of the unit p needs of the
names it exports, as Core: each type it mentions declared, and each
value imported.

Each exported value is an import at its type, and each exported type
and every type the exports' types mention, through the types' own
fields, is declared as p declares it, in p's order; a name p does not
declare is a built-in type's, or another unit's the client has.

members.name: fingerprints
members.spec: val fingerprints : (string -> string) -> Core.program -> (string * string) list
members.doc:
`fingerprints hash iface` is each declaration of the interface by its
name with its fingerprint, which moves where what a client reads of it
moves.

A type's is its recursive group's: the hash of the group's
declarations and of the fingerprints of the types outside it that they
mention, so that a group hashes as one. A value's is the hash of its
type and of the fingerprints of the types it mentions. A type no
declaration of the interface gives is its name.

HS_AST.doc:
The abstract syntax of Haskell 98, the Report's chapter 10, before
names and fixity are resolved (the haskell98 roadmap's D28).

It keeps what the source says: a span on every node, parentheses as
nodes, operators in flat sequences with negation as an item (fixity is
resolved after names, D29), literals and contexts as written. Every
node also has an annotation that holds its own tokens, those of the
source that are not in a node below it, each with the trivia before
it: comments, pragmas, white space, and the braces and semicolons of
layout, written or not. From the annotations `HsPrint.exact` prints a
module as its file, byte for byte. A node that a tool makes has
`noAnn`, and is printed as `HsPrint.explicit` prints it.

Patterns are read relaxed and checked after, so a sequence of patterns
with operators, `PSeq`, holds constructor operators only, and `PJux`
never leaves the parser.

members.name: tok
members.spec: type tok = {trivia : HsToken.trivium list, start : int, stop : int}
members.doc:
A token of the source as a node owns it: the bytes it covers, none
for one of layout's, and the trivia before it.

members.name: ann
members.spec: type ann = {span : HsSource.span, toks : tok list}
members.doc:
A node's annotation: its span, and its own tokens in the order of the
source.

members.name: noAnn
members.doc:
The annotation of a node that no source gave, and of every node of a
tree read with annotations off.

members.name: qname
members.doc:
A name as written: its qualifier, `""` for none, and the name. The
special constructors are names too: `()`, `[]`, `(,)`, `(,,)` and on,
`(->)`, and `:`.

members.name: name
members.spec: datatype name = Name of ann * qname
members.doc:
An identifier or an operator of the source, with its annotation,
whose tokens are the parentheses or backquotes around it, if any,
and the name.

members.name: lit_
members.spec:
datatype lit_ =
    LInt of IntInf.int * string
  | LFloat of string
  | LChar of int * string
  | LString of int list * string
members.doc: A literal: its value, and its text as written.

members.name: lit
members.spec: datatype lit = Lit of ann * lit_
members.doc: A literal of the source.

members.name: qop
members.spec: datatype qop = VarOp of name | ConOp of name
members.doc:
An operator where an operator goes: a variable's, `+` or `` `div` ``,
or a constructor's, `:+` or `` `Cons` ``.

members.name: ty
members.spec: datatype ty = T of ann * ty_
members.doc: A type, a context among them, as written.

members.name: ty_
members.spec:
datatype ty_ =
    TVar of name
  | TCon of name
  | TApp of ty * ty
  | TFun of ty * ty
  | TList of ty
  | TTuple of ty list
  | TParen of ty
members.doc: The forms of a type.

members.name: pat
members.spec: datatype pat = P of ann * pat_
members.doc: A pattern.

members.name: pat_
members.spec:
datatype pat_ =
    PVar of name
  | PWild
  | PLit of lit
  | PNegLit of lit
  | PCon of name * pat list
  | PRec of name * (name * pat) list
  | PTuple of pat list
  | PList of pat list
  | PParen of pat
  | PAs of name * pat
  | PLazy of pat
  | PNPlusK of name * lit
  | PSeq of patitem list
  | PJux of pat list
members.doc: The forms of a pattern.

members.name: patitem
members.spec: datatype patitem = PA of pat | PO of qop
members.doc: An item of a sequence of patterns.

members.name: exp
members.spec: datatype exp = E of ann * exp_
members.doc: An expression.

members.name: exp_
members.spec:
datatype exp_ =
    EVar of name
  | ECon of name
  | ELit of lit
  | EApp of exp * exp
  | ESeq of expitem list
  | ELam of pat list * exp
  | ELet of decl list * exp
  | EIf of exp * exp * exp
  | ECase of exp * alt list
  | EDo of stmt list
  | ETuple of exp list
  | EParen of exp
  | EList of exp list
  | EEnum of exp * exp option * exp option
  | EComp of exp * stmt list
  | ELeftSec of exp * qop
  | ERightSec of qop * exp
  | ERecCon of name * (name * exp) list
  | ERecUpd of exp * (name * exp) list
  | ESig of exp * ty option * ty
members.doc: The forms of an expression.

members.name: expitem
members.spec: datatype expitem = EA of exp | EO of qop | ENeg
members.doc: An item of a sequence: an operand, an operator, or `-` as negation.

members.name: stmt
members.spec: datatype stmt = S of ann * stmt_
members.doc: A statement of `do`, or a qualifier of a comprehension.

members.name: stmt_
members.spec:
datatype stmt_ =
    SBind of pat * exp
  | SLet of decl list
  | SExp of exp
members.doc: The forms of a statement.

members.name: alt
members.spec: datatype alt = Alt of ann * pat * rhs
members.doc:
An alternative of `case`: `p rhs`, where the right-hand side's
arrow is `->`.

members.name: rhs
members.spec: datatype rhs = Rhs of ann * rhs_
members.doc: A right-hand side: an expression or guards, with a `where`.

members.name: rhs_
members.spec:
datatype rhs_ =
    Plain of exp * decl list option
  | Guarded of guard list * decl list option
members.doc: The forms of a right-hand side.

members.name: guard
members.spec: datatype guard = Guard of ann * exp * exp
members.doc: A guard and its expression: `| g = e`.

members.name: funlhs
members.spec: datatype funlhs = F of ann * funlhs_
members.doc: The left-hand side of a function's equation.

members.name: funlhs_
members.spec:
datatype funlhs_ =
    FPrefix of name * pat list
  | FInfix of pat * qop * pat
  | FParen of funlhs * pat list
members.doc: The forms of a left-hand side.

members.name: decl
members.spec: datatype decl = D of ann * decl_
members.doc: A declaration.

members.name: decl_
members.spec:
datatype decl_ =
    DSig of name list * ty option * ty
  | DFixity of fixity * lit option * qop list
  | DFun of funlhs * rhs
  | DPat of pat * rhs
  | DType of name * name list * ty
  | DData of ty option * name * name list * constr list * deriv option
  | DNewtype of ty option * name * name list * constr * deriv option
  | DClass of ty option * name * name * decl list option
  | DInstance of ty option * name * ty * decl list option
  | DDefault of ty list
members.doc: The forms of a declaration.

members.name: fixity
members.doc: The associativity of a fixity declaration.

members.name: constr
members.spec: datatype constr = C of ann * constr_
members.doc: A constructor of `data` or `newtype`.

members.name: constr_
members.spec:
datatype constr_ =
    CPlain of name * (bool * ty) list
  | CInfix of (bool * ty) * name * (bool * ty)
  | CRec of name * field list
members.doc: The forms of a constructor.

members.name: field
members.spec: datatype field = Field of ann * name list * bool * ty
members.doc: The fields of a record constructor that one type has.

members.name: deriv
members.spec: datatype deriv = Deriv of ann * bool * name list
members.doc:
A `deriving` clause: whether its classes are in parentheses, and
them.

members.name: entity
members.spec: datatype entity = Ent of ann * entity_
members.doc: What an export or an import names.

members.name: entity_
members.spec:
datatype entity_ =
    EntVar of name
  | EntType of name * sub option
  | EntModule of name
members.doc: The forms of an entity.

members.name: sub
members.spec: datatype sub = SubAll | SubList of name list
members.doc: The constructors or methods an entity names: `(..)`, or a list.

members.name: import
members.spec:
datatype import = Import of ann * {qualified : bool, module : name, as_ : name option, hiding : bool,
                                   spec : entity list option}
members.doc: An import declaration.

members.name: module
members.spec:
datatype module = Module of ann * {name : name option, exports : entity list option,
                                   imports : import list, decls : decl list}
members.doc:
A module: its header, if any, its imports and its declarations. The
annotation's last token covers no byte and holds the trivia at the end
of the file.

members.name: qname
members.doc:
`qname (qual, name)` is the name `name` qualified by `qual`, `""` for
none.

members.name: nameText
members.doc:
`nameText q` is the name as the source writes it in a variable's
place, qualified: M.x for `x` of `M`, or `+`.

members.name: isSymbolic
members.doc:
`isSymbolic q` is whether the name of `q` is an operator's rather
than an identifier's: its first character is a symbol or `:`.

The special constructors but `:` are not.

members.name: isSpecial
members.doc:
`isSpecial q` is whether `q` is one of the special constructors that
are written with brackets: `()`, `[]`, the tuples', `(->)`.

members.name: spanOfExp
members.doc:
`spanOfExp e`, `spanOfPat p`, `spanOfTy t` and `spanOfDecl d` are the
spans of the nodes.

members.name: spanOfPat
members.doc:
`spanOfExp e`, `spanOfPat p`, `spanOfTy t` and `spanOfDecl d` are the
spans of the nodes.

members.name: spanOfTy
members.doc:
`spanOfExp e`, `spanOfPat p`, `spanOfTy t` and `spanOfDecl d` are the
spans of the nodes.

members.name: spanOfDecl
members.doc:
`spanOfExp e`, `spanOfPat p`, `spanOfTy t` and `spanOfDecl d` are the
spans of the nodes.

HS_CHAR.doc:
The classes of characters of the Haskell 98 Report's lexical syntax
(chapter 2, section 9.2), by code point.

Above ASCII the Report's classes are those of Unicode's general
category: `uniSmall` a lowercase letter, `uniLarge` an uppercase or
titlecase one, `uniDigit` a decimal digit, `uniSymbol` a symbol or a
punctuation mark, `uniWhite` a space, by the general category of
Rune's `lib/unicode` (the haskell98 roadmap's D21). A character of no
class, a letter of no case (Lo, Lm), a mark, a number not decimal, a
control or a format character, is refused outside a comment or a
literal; the lexer reads any character in a comment or a literal (the
reading R5).

members.name: class
members.spec:
datatype class =
    Small
  | Large
  | Digit
  | Symbol
  | White
  | Special
  | Colon
  | Quote
  | Unknown
members.doc: A class of the lexical syntax.

members.name: classify
members.doc:
`classify c` is the class of the code point `c`; `Unknown` for a
negative `c`.

members.name: isIdent
members.doc:
`isIdent c` is whether `c` may continue an identifier: a small or a
large letter, a digit or `'`.

members.name: isSymbol
members.doc: `isSymbol c` is whether `c` may continue an operator: a symbol or `:`.

HS_CLASSES.doc:
The classes and instances of Haskell 98's checker (the haskell98
roadmap's M13; the Report's 4.3): every class and instance of the
program, for entailment. Instances are not names: every instance a
program declares, or derives, is in force in all of it.

members.name: class
members.spec: type class = {key : string, supers : string list, methods : string list, kind : HsTypes.kind}
members.doc:
A class: its key, its direct superclasses, its methods' keys, in
order, and the kind of its variable.

members.name: instance
members.spec:
type instance = {id : string, cls : string, tycon : string, vars : int, ctx : HsTypes.pred list,
                 derived : bool, home : string}
members.doc:
An instance `C (T a1 ... an)`: its identity, class, type constructor
and the number of its head's variables.

With them, its context over `TGen 0` to `TGen (n - 1)`, whether it is
derived, and the module that declares it.

members.name: env
members.doc: The classes and instances of a program.

members.name: empty
members.doc: No class and no instance.

members.name: addClass
members.doc: `addClass (env, c)` is `env` with the class `c`.

members.name: addInstance
members.doc: `addInstance (env, i)` is `env` with the instance `i`.

members.name: withContext
members.spec: val withContext : env * string * HsTypes.pred list -> env
members.doc:
`withContext (env, id, ctx)` is `env` with the context of the
instance `id` replaced, as deriving's fixpoint does.

members.name: findClass
members.spec: val findClass : env * string -> class option
members.doc: `findClass (env, key)` is the class of `key`.

members.name: findInstance
members.spec: val findInstance : env * string * string -> instance option
members.doc:
`findInstance (env, cls, tycon)` is the instance of `cls` at `tycon`,
a read of the instance's, found or not (HsUsage, H2).

members.name: instances
members.doc: `instances env` is every instance of `env`.

members.name: classList
members.doc: `classList env` is every class of `env`.

members.name: instanceId
members.doc:
`instanceId (cls, tycon)` is the identity of the instance of `cls`
at `tycon`.

members.name: showInstance
members.doc:
`showInstance id` is the instance `id` as a message names it: its
class and its type constructor.

members.name: superPath
members.spec: val superPath : env * string * string -> string list option
members.doc:
`superPath (env, c, s)` is the classes from `c` to its superclass `s`,
`c` first and `s` last.

Each is the direct superclass of the one before; NONE where `s` is no
superclass of `c`.

members.name: superclasses
members.spec: val superclasses : env * string -> string list
members.doc: `superclasses (env, c)` is every superclass of `c`, through.

HS_DERIVE.doc:
Haskell 98's derived instances (the Report's chapter 10; the haskell98
roadmap's M14, D33's C): the methods of a derived `Eq`, `Ord`, `Enum`,
`Bounded`, `Ix`, `Show` or `Read` instance, made as the renamed tree a
user would write, with chapter 10's text as the specification, so that
the checker elaborates them as it does a user's instance and HsLint
checks them as any instance (D54).

The checker infers the instance's context (10.1, HsInfer) and checks
what this makes. The tree names entities, not text: a derived `Ix` in
Time uses methods Time does not import (E16). Records are shown and
read as `C {f = v}` at precedence 11 (R41, GHC's row, which Haskell
2010 took); an infix constructor by its fixity (10.4).

members.name: constr
members.spec:
type constr = {name : HsAst.name, arity : int, fields : HsAst.name list, isInfix : bool,
               fixity : HsAst.fixity * int}
members.doc:
A constructor of the data type, as deriving reads it.

Its name, as the renamed tree has it, the number of its fields,
their names for a record, whether it is declared infix
(`isInfix`), and its fixity.

members.name: methods
members.spec:
val methods : {cls : string, constrs : constr list, entity : string * string -> string option, file : string}
              -> HsAst.decl list option
members.doc:
`methods {cls, constrs, entity, file}` is the method bindings of the
derived instance of the class `cls`, a key, at the data type of
`constrs`.

`entity (space, name)` is the key of a standard entity by name,
`"v"` or `"t"`: the Prelude's, and Ix's `range`, `index`, `inRange`
and `rangeSize`. `file` names the nodes' spans, each of its own, so
that the evidence of each is apart; NONE where `cls` is no class
that can be derived.

HS_DESUGAR.doc:
Desugaring to Core (the haskell98 roadmap's M15, D34): a checked
program made the Core program it means.

The program's renamed and resolved trees and the checker's evidence
records (D31) are translated by chapter 3's translations and 4.4.3's,
taken literally (`-O0`, D34's A), with dictionaries for classes.

- Expressions: a literal is `fromInteger` or `fromRational` of its value
  (3.2), but where the checker chose the Prelude's `Int`, `Integer`,
  `Float` or `Double`, whose value it is; `e1 op e2` is `(op) e1 e2`
  and `-e` the Prelude's `negate` (3.4); a section is a lambda, its
  operand bound once outside it (3.5, R11's sharing); `if` a `case` on
  `True` and `False` (3.6); a list the constructors it abbreviates
  (3.7); an arithmetic sequence the method of `Enum` (3.10); a list
  comprehension `concatMap` over a local `ok` (3.11); `let` a `let` or
  a `letrec` by dependency, a pattern binding each of its variables a
  lazy match of its own (3.12, rule (d)); `do` `>>=`, `>>` and `fail`
  (3.14); records by their constructors' fields (3.15); `e :: t` a
  binding of its own scheme (3.16); a string literal unpacked lazily
  by the runtime (D24).
- Bindings: a function's clauses one lambda of as many parameters as
  its patterns, matched in the Report's order (4.4.3.1, HsMatch); a
  guarded binding falls to the next clause, or for a pattern binding to
  an error (4.4.3.2); a binding the checker generalised a type lambda
  over its variables and a lambda over its dictionaries, in the order
  of its scheme, so that every use is the variable at its types and its
  dictionaries, as the use's record gives them.
- Classes and instances: a class the data type of its dictionaries,
  with a selector for each method and each direct superclass, and a
  value for each default method; an instance a function of its
  context's dictionaries giving its dictionary, a method it does not
  define its class's default, or an error where there is none (4.3.2).
- A strict constructor used as a value forces its strict arguments,
  the last first (4.2.1, defect 17); a newtype's constructor is a cast.
- `main` is the program's main as Core's `main` wants it.

The names a translation uses are the Prelude's entities, whatever a
program defines (3, E9): `translationNames` lists them, with Ratio's
`:%`, for a cache's key (H9).

members.name: module_
members.spec: type module_ = {id : string, ast : HsAst.module, library : bool}
members.doc:
A module of the program: its identity, its renamed tree with fixity
resolved, and whether it is the library's.

members.name: program
members.spec:
val program : {modules : module_ list, groups : string list list, infer : HsInfer.env, evidence : HsEvidence.table,
               derived : (string * string * HsAst.decl list) list, prelude : string * string -> string option,
               entity : string * string * string -> string, runtime : Core.program, leaves : (string * string list) list,
               main : string}
              -> Core.program
members.doc:
`program {modules, groups, infer, evidence, derived, prelude, entity, runtime, leaves, main}` is the Core program of the checked `modules`.

The modules are every module of the program and of the library it
reaches, in `groups`, their strongly connected groups by identity in
order, each desugared as a unit after those before it (`unit`). Their
checking left the environment `infer`, the records `evidence` and the
methods of the derived instances, `derived`, each with its module and
its instance's identity (HsDerive, M14), which are desugared as a
written instance's.

`prelude` and `entity` find what the translations name (HsDsEnv);
`runtime` is rhc's runtime in Core, whose types it is written against
and which it does not repeat; `leaves` are the modules of primitives
that no file holds, each with what it exports, the runtime's values of
those names; `main` is the key of the program's `main`. The result
holds what `main` reaches, and the data types it names, each body made
only where `main` reaches it.

**Raises** `Fail` for what the checker should have refused, or a form
this desugaring does not take, with a message.

members.name: interface
members.doc:
What a unit's desugaring leaves the units after it.

`core` is its types and its values as imports (`(import x TYPE)`);
`primTypes` each type of the library with no constructor, by key, made
Core's own, and `builtinCons` Bool's constructors, Core's; `fields`
each constructor's fields' keys (`""` for one with no name), and
`constructors` each data type's constructors' keys, in order; `leaves`
the keys of the leaves' values, and `defaults` the methods with a
default (a `%dm:` value); `forced` each constructor with a strict field
of a newtype's type, lazy in Core, by the fields it forces where it is
applied (HsDsCore.forced).

members.name: unit
members.spec:
val unit : {interfaces : interface list, modules : module_ list, infer : HsInfer.env, evidence : HsEvidence.table,
            derived : (string * string * HsAst.decl list) list, prelude : string * string -> string option,
            entity : string * string * string -> string, runtime : Core.program, leaves : (string * string list) list,
            main : string option}
           -> Core.program * interface
members.doc:
`unit p` is the Core of the unit of the modules of `p`, after the units
of its interfaces, in order, and its interface.

The Core is its types, a copy of each type of the units before that it
names, an import of each of their values that it names, and every
value it defines; the runtime's names are left to the runtime's unit.
`infer` and `evidence` are a checking that holds the unit's modules and
what they import; `leaves` is the first unit's, and `main`, the key of
the program's `main`, the unit's that defines it, whose Core then has
Core's `main`. The rest is as `program` takes it.

members.name: library
members.doc:
The library's units, desugared once (D45's saved world), each value's
body made the first time it is wanted.

members.name: library
members.spec:
val library : {modules : module_ list, groups : string list list, infer : HsInfer.env, evidence : HsEvidence.table,
               derived : (string * string * HsAst.decl list) list, prelude : string * string -> string option,
               entity : string * string * string -> string, runtime : Core.program, leaves : (string * string list) list}
              -> library
members.doc:
`library p` is the units of the groups of `p` that hold modules marked
`library`.

`p` is a checking of the library alone (every instance of its
environment is the library's), in `program`'s form without `main`.

members.name: prepare
members.doc:
`prepare lib` makes every body of `lib` now, as a saved world keeps
them; a body that fails is failed again where a program reaches it.

members.name: programOn
members.spec:
val programOn : library * {modules : module_ list, groups : string list list, infer : HsInfer.env,
                           evidence : HsEvidence.table, derived : (string * string * HsAst.decl list) list,
                           prelude : string * string -> string option, entity : string * string * string -> string,
                           main : string}
                -> Core.program
members.doc:
`programOn (lib, p)` is `program` of `p` with the library's units
`lib`: the groups of `p` that hold no module of the library desugared
after them.

The modules, environment, records and derived instances of `p` are the
whole checking's, the library's among them, as `program` takes them;
a value of the library is `lib`'s.

members.name: translationNames
members.doc:
`translationNames` is each entity the translations name, by its
space, its module and its name.

members.name: missingPrimitives
members.doc:
`missingPrimitives ()` is each primitive of the library that the last
desugaring found neither in Core nor in the runtime, or of another
type.

It is of the bodies the desugaring made, the library's made once among
them.

Each is an error where it is used.

HS_DS_CORE.doc:
Core as desugaring builds it (the haskell98 roadmap's M15): each
expression with its type.

An expression is made with its type, worked out from its parts as
CoreLint works it out, so that an argument that is not an atom can be
bound by a `let` of its type; and the declarations of the program being
built are kept, by which a constructor's fields and a newtype's
unfolding are known.

A name made here starts with `%`, which no name of Haskell's holds,
neither a top-level entity's nor a local's (`x#3`).

members.name: texp
members.doc: An expression and its type.

members.name: shape
members.spec:
datatype shape =
    DataS of (string * Core.ty list) list
  | NewS of string * Core.ty
  | PrimS
members.doc: What a type constructor of the program is.

members.name: reset
members.doc: `reset ()` forgets every declaration and starts the names again.

members.name: fresh
members.doc: `fresh base` is a new name, `%base` and a number.

members.name: saved
members.doc:
What is known of the declarations, kept: so that a desugaring of the
library's modules, made once, is where each program's starts.

members.name: save
members.doc: `save ()` is what is known now.

members.name: restore
members.doc: `restore s` makes `s` what is known.

members.name: canonical
members.doc:
`canonical e` is `e` with each name made here that it binds numbered
again, from 1 in the order they are bound, its base kept.

So a value's Core is the same whatever was made before it.

members.name: declare
members.doc:
`declare d` adds the data type, newtype, value or import `d` to what is
known.

A value is known by its type.

members.name: tupleArity
members.doc:
`tupleArity c` is the number of components of the tuple whose type and
constructor are named `c`, `(,...,)`.

A tuple is of arbitrary length (3.8): one not declared is declared
where it is first wanted, by `tycon`, `conInfo` and the other lookups,
and `valueType` gives its constructor as a function its type.

members.name: tupleData
members.doc: `tupleData n` is the declaration of the tuple of `n` components.

members.name: tycon
members.spec: val tycon : string -> ((string * Core.kind) list * shape) option
members.doc:
`tycon c` is the parameters and the shape of the type constructor `c`,
Core's built-in ones among them.

members.name: conInfo
members.spec: val conInfo : string -> {tycon : string, params : (string * Core.kind) list, fields : Core.ty list} option
members.doc:
`conInfo k` is the type constructor of the constructor `k`, its
parameters and its fields' types over them.

members.name: fieldsAt
members.spec: val fieldsAt : string * Core.ty list -> Core.ty list
members.doc:
`fieldsAt (k, args)` is the types of the fields of the constructor `k`
of a type applied to `args`.

**Raises** `Fail` where `k` is not declared.

members.name: valueType
members.doc:
`valueType x` is the type of the value `x` of the top level, or of
rhc's runtime.

members.name: unfold
members.doc: `unfold t` is `t` unfolded once, where a newtype is at its head.

members.name: dataArgs
members.spec: val dataArgs : Core.ty -> (string * Core.ty list) option
members.doc:
`dataArgs t` is the type constructor at the head of `t`, a data type's
or a newtype's, and its arguments.

members.name: kindOf
members.spec: val kindOf : (string * Core.kind) list * Core.ty -> Core.kind
members.doc:
`kindOf (vars, t)` is the kind of the type `t`, whose variables have
the kinds `vars` or are of `*`.

members.name: inferKinds
members.spec: val inferKinds : string list * (string -> Core.kind option) * Core.ty list -> (string * Core.kind) list
members.doc:
`inferKinds (vars, known, tys)` is the kind of each of `vars`, which
the types `tys` of kind `*` hold.

Each is worked out from where it stands, and is `*` where nothing
says; `known` gives the kinds of the other variables.

members.name: instantiate
members.spec: val instantiate : Core.ty * Core.ty list -> Core.ty
members.doc:
`instantiate (t, tys)` is `t` without its first foralls, their
variables replaced by `tys`, in order.

members.name: applyType
members.spec: val applyType : Core.ty * Core.arg list -> Core.ty
members.doc:
`applyType (t, args)` is the type of a function of type `t` given
`args`.

members.name: params
members.spec: val params : Core.ty * int -> Core.ty list * Core.ty
members.doc:
`params (t, n)` is the types of the first `n` parameters of a
function of type `t`, and the type of what it gives then.

**Raises** `Fail` where `t` takes fewer.

members.name: lazyTy
members.doc: `lazyTy t` is `t` as a lazy binding holds it: without `!`.

members.name: atom
members.spec: val atom : texp * (Core.atom * Core.ty -> texp) -> texp
members.doc:
`atom (x, k)` gives `k` the atom of `x`: itself where it is one,
otherwise a variable bound to it by a lazy `let`.

members.name: atoms
members.spec: val atoms : texp list * ((Core.atom * Core.ty) list -> texp) -> texp
members.doc: `atoms (xs, k)` is `atom` over each of `xs`, left to right.

members.name: var
members.doc: `var (x, t)` is the variable `x` of type `t`.

members.name: app
members.spec: val app : texp * Core.arg list -> texp
members.doc:
`app (f, args)` is `f` applied to `args`; `f` itself where there are
none.

members.name: appAtoms
members.spec: val appAtoms : texp * texp list -> texp
members.doc:
`appAtoms (f, xs)` is `f` applied to the atoms of `xs`, each bound by
`atom`.

members.name: lam
members.spec: val lam : Core.binder list * texp -> texp
members.doc:
`lam (binders, body)` is a lambda of `binders`; `body` itself where
there are none.

members.name: let_
members.spec: val let_ : string * Core.ty * texp * texp -> texp
members.doc: `let_ (x, t, rhs, body)` is `let x : t = rhs in body`, `t` lazy.

members.name: letrec
members.spec: val letrec : (string * Core.ty * texp) list * texp -> texp
members.doc:
`letrec (bs, body)` binds `bs`, each with its lazy type, in each
other and in `body`; `body` itself where there are none.

members.name: force
members.spec: val force : texp * (string * Core.ty -> texp) -> texp
members.doc:
`force (x, k)` evaluates `x` by a `case` and gives `k` the evaluated
variable and its type.

members.name: forceRep
members.doc:
`forceRep (x, k)` evaluates `x`'s representation, through every newtype
at its head, by casts, before `k ()`: what a strict field of a newtype's
type forces.

members.name: forced
members.doc:
`forced k` is whether each field of the constructor `k` is forced where
it is applied: its `!`, or a strict field of a newtype's type, lazy in
Core (`setForced`).

members.name: setForced
members.spec: val setForced : string * bool list -> unit
members.doc:
`setForced (k, flags)` gives the constructor `k` the fields it forces,
where they are not its fields' `!`.

members.name: forcedOverrides
members.spec: val forcedOverrides : unit -> (string * bool list) list
members.doc: `forcedOverrides ()` is each constructor `setForced` gave its flags.

members.name: caseCon
members.spec: val caseCon : Core.atom * Core.ty * (string * ((string * Core.ty) list -> texp)) list * texp option -> texp
members.doc:
`caseCon (x, ty, alts, default)` is a `case` on the atom `x` of the
data type `ty`.

It has an alternative for each constructor of `alts`, made of its
fields' names and types, and `default` for the others, left out where
`alts` covers them all.

**Raises** `Fail` where `ty` is not a data type.

members.name: ifBool
members.spec: val ifBool : texp * texp * texp -> texp
members.doc: `ifBool (c, t, e)` is `case c of True -> t; False -> e`.

members.name: con
members.spec: val con : string * Core.ty list * texp list -> texp
members.doc:
`con (k, tys, xs)` is the constructor `k` at the types `tys` applied
to the atoms of `xs`.

members.name: cast
members.doc: `cast (x, t)` is `x` cast to the type `t`, into or out of a newtype.

members.name: fail
members.spec: val fail : string * string * Core.ty -> texp
members.doc:
`fail (kind, message, t)` is an expression of type `t` that raises
the exception the primitive `kind` makes of `message`.

`kind` is `exn_pattern` for a match that fails, `exn_error` for
`error`'s. It calls one of `raisers`, at `t`.

members.name: mentions
members.doc:
`mentions (x, e)` is whether the variable `x` occurs in `e`, which
binds no other `x`.

members.name: names
members.doc:
`names e` is every variable `e` holds, bound in it or not, and every
constructor, each once.

members.name: raisers
members.doc:
`raisers` is the values `fail` calls, a declaration each, which a
program that uses `fail` holds.

members.name: unitTy
members.doc: `unitTy` is the type of Haskell's `()`, rhc's runtime's.

members.name: unitVal
members.doc: `unitVal ()` is the value `()`.

HS_DS_ENV.doc:
What desugaring knows of a checked program (the haskell98 roadmap's
M15): its names, types, records and dictionaries in Core.

It holds the names the program's entities have in Core, its types made
Core's, the checker's evidence records (D31) by node, its dictionaries,
and the primitives of rhc's library made functions of Haskell's types.

An entity of the top level is named in Core by its module's identity, a
dot and its name, haskell98:Prelude.map or Main.f; a local keeps the
renamer's unique name, x\#3. What desugaring makes has a name starting
with %: a class's dictionary constructor, %dict:C, an instance's
dictionary function, %inst:C@T, a superclass's selector, %super:C\>S, a
class's default method, %dm:m.

Types: a type constructor of the program is named as its entity; the
Prelude's `Bool` is Core's `Bool`, and a type that a module of the
library declares with no constructor is Core's own (`Int`, `Integer`,
`Char`, `Float`, `Double`, `Str`, `Ref`), PreludeIO's `IOError` Core's
`Exn`, and `IO` the newtype `IO` over `World -> (utuple World a)` (D25),
a type constructor of its own so that `Monad IO` has a dictionary. A
class is the data type of its dictionaries, of the same name: its
direct superclasses' dictionaries, then its methods, each of the type
of its own scheme.

members.name: program
members.spec:
type program = {infer : HsInfer.env, evidence : HsEvidence.table, prelude : string * string -> string option,
                library : string -> bool, entity : string * string * string -> string}
members.doc:
What a desugaring is given: the checker's environment and records, and
how to find the entities the translations name.

They are the checker's environment after the last unit, its evidence
records, the key of what the Prelude exports by space (`"v"` or `"t"`)
and name, whether a module's identity is the library's, and the key of
an entity of a module of the library by its space, the module's name
and its name: Ratio's `:%`, which a floating literal is made of, though
the Prelude does not export it (E9).

members.name: start
members.doc: `start p` makes `p` the program desugared, forgetting the last.

members.name: continue
members.doc:
`continue p` makes `p` the program desugared, keeping what is known of
its types and constructors: a program's, after its library's.

members.name: saved
members.doc: What is known of the types and constructors, kept.

members.name: save
members.doc: `save ()` is what is known now.

members.name: restore
members.doc: `restore s` makes `s` what is known.

members.name: known
members.spec:
type known = {primTypes : (string * string) list, builtinCons : (string * string) list,
              fields : (string * string list) list}
members.doc:
What is known of the types and constructors, as lists, for a unit's
interface.

Each type of the library made Core's own, by key, Bool's constructors,
and each constructor's fields, by key.

members.name: known
members.doc: `known ()` is what is known now, each list by key.

members.name: learn
members.doc: `learn k` adds `k` to what is known.

members.name: classes
members.doc: `classes ()` is the program's classes and instances.

members.name: valueScheme
members.doc: `valueScheme key` is the type the checker gave the value `key`.

members.name: prelude
members.doc:
`prelude (space, name)` is the key of what the Prelude exports.

**Raises** `Fail` where it exports no such name, a fault of the
library.

members.name: isLibrary
members.doc:
`isLibrary id` is whether the module of identity `id` is the
library's.

members.name: libraryEntity
members.spec: val libraryEntity : string * string * string -> string
members.doc:
`libraryEntity (space, module, name)` is the key of an entity of a
module of the library.

members.name: setFields
members.spec: val setFields : string * string list -> unit
members.doc:
`setFields (con, fields)` records the fields of the constructor
`con`, by their keys in order, `""` for one without a name.

members.name: fieldsOf
members.doc: `fieldsOf con` is the fields of the constructor `con`.

members.name: coreName
members.doc: `coreName key` is the Core name of the entity `key`.

members.name: valueKey
members.doc:
`valueKey n` is the key of the value the name `n` of the renamed tree
stands for.

It is a top-level entity's key, a local's own name, or a built-in
constructor's (`()`, `[]`, `:`, `(,)`).

members.name: homeOf
members.doc: `homeOf key` and `nameOf key` are the parts of an entity's key.

members.name: nameOf
members.doc: `homeOf key` and `nameOf key` are the parts of an entity's key.

members.name: tyconName
members.doc:
`tyconName key` is the type constructor of Core that the type
constructor `key` is.

members.name: conName
members.doc:
`conName key` is the constructor of Core that the data constructor
`key` is.

members.name: primType
members.doc:
`primType (key, core)` makes the type `key`, which a module of the
library declares with no constructor, Core's type `core`.

members.name: isPrimType
members.doc: `isPrimType key` is whether the type `key` is Core's own.

members.name: builtinCon
members.doc:
`builtinCon (key, core)` makes the constructor `key` Core's `core`,
as the Prelude's `True` is Core's.

members.name: dictCon
members.doc:
`dictCon cls` is the constructor of the dictionaries of the class
`cls`.

members.name: dfunName
members.doc: `dfunName id` is the dictionary function of the instance `id`.

members.name: superName
members.doc:
`superName (cls, super)` is the selector of the superclass `super`
from a dictionary of `cls`.

members.name: defaultName
members.doc: `defaultName method` is the default of the method `method`.

members.name: env
members.doc:
What is in scope where an expression is desugared.

It holds the variables, each the atom of Core it is and its type,
dictionary parameters among them, and the type variables with their
kinds.

members.name: empty
members.doc: `empty` is the scope of the top level.

members.name: bind
members.spec: val bind : env * string * Core.atom * Core.ty -> env
members.doc:
`bind (env, x, atom, t)` is `env` with `x` the atom `atom` of type
`t`.

members.name: lookup
members.spec: val lookup : env * string -> (Core.atom * Core.ty) option
members.doc: `lookup (env, x)` is the atom `x` is and its type.

members.name: bindTypes
members.spec: val bindTypes : env * (string * Core.kind) list -> env
members.doc: `bindTypes (env, vars)` is `env` with the type variables `vars`.

members.name: typeVars
members.doc: `typeVars env` is the type variables in scope.

members.name: ty
members.doc:
`ty env t` is the Core type of `t`, a closed type of the records.

A rigid variable not in scope stands for nothing a value can be of, a
variable of another binding of a group that this one's type does not
hold, and is `()`.

members.name: tyGen
members.spec: val tyGen : env * Core.ty list -> HsTypes.ty -> Core.ty
members.doc:
`tyGen (env, gens) t` is the Core type of `t`, whose `TGen i` is the
`i`th of `gens`.

members.name: predTy
members.doc: `predTy env p` is the type of the dictionaries of the predicate `p`.

members.name: scheme
members.spec: val scheme : env -> HsEvidence.scheme -> Core.ty * (string * Core.kind) list
members.doc:
`scheme env s` is the type of a value of the scheme `s` of the
records, and its variables with their kinds.

The type is a forall over its variables, with their kinds, of a
function of its context's dictionaries, in order, giving its type.

members.name: genScheme
members.doc:
`genScheme s` is the type of a value of the checker's scheme `s`, its
variables named `g1`, `g2` and on.

members.name: ioTy
members.doc: `ioTy t` is `IO t`.

members.name: records
members.spec: val records : string * HsSource.span -> HsEvidence.record list
members.doc: `records (kind, span)` is the records at a node.

members.name: useOf
members.spec: val useOf : HsSource.span -> {tys : HsTypes.ty list, dicts : HsEvidence.dict list}
members.doc:
`useOf span` is the types and dictionaries of the variable or
constructor used at `span`.

members.name: bindOf
members.doc: `bindOf span` is the record of the binder at `span`.

members.name: overloadedOf
members.spec: val overloadedOf : string * HsSource.span -> HsTypes.ty * (string * HsEvidence.dict) list
members.doc:
`overloadedOf (kind, span)` is the type and the dictionaries by class
of a construct the Report translates through a class.

members.name: dict
members.doc: `dict env d` is the dictionary `d`.

members.name: instantiate
members.spec: val instantiate : env -> HsDsCore.texp * HsTypes.ty list * HsEvidence.dict list -> HsDsCore.texp
members.doc:
`instantiate env (f, tys, dicts)` is `f` at the types `tys` and the
dictionaries `dicts`, as a use's record gives them.

members.name: global
members.doc:
`global key` is the value `key` of the top level, at its type, before
any is given it.

members.name: method
members.spec: val method : env -> string * Core.ty list * HsDsCore.texp list -> HsDsCore.texp
members.doc:
`method env (key, tys, dicts)` is the value `key`, a method of the
Prelude's or a function, at the Core types `tys` and the dictionaries
`dicts`.

members.name: superDict
members.spec: val superDict : env -> HsEvidence.dict * string * string -> HsEvidence.dict
members.doc:
`superDict env (d, cls, super)` is the dictionary of `super`, a
superclass of `cls`, taken from `d`, a dictionary of `cls`.

It goes by the path of direct superclasses between them.

members.name: integerLit
members.spec: val integerLit : env -> IntInf.int * HsTypes.ty * HsEvidence.dict -> HsDsCore.texp
members.doc:
`integerLit env (i, t, num)` is the integer literal `i` at the type
`t`, of which `num` is the `Num` dictionary.

It is `fromInteger i` (3.2), but an `Int` in range or an `Integer`
itself, where `num` is the Prelude's instance at that type.

members.name: rationalLit
members.spec: val rationalLit : env -> string * HsTypes.ty * HsEvidence.dict -> HsDsCore.texp
members.doc:
`rationalLit env (text, t, fractional)` is the floating literal
written `text` at the type `t`.

It is `fromRational` of Ratio's `n :% d`, `n/d` its value in lowest
terms (3.2), but a `Double` or a `Float` itself where `fractional` is
the Prelude's instance at that type.

members.name: stringLit
members.doc:
`stringLit chars` is a string literal of the code points `chars`.

Its bytes in UTF-8 are unpacked lazily by the runtime's
`primUnpackString` (D24's A).

members.name: toHaskell
members.doc:
`toHaskell (x, want)` is `x`, a value of a type of Core's own making,
as a value of `want`, the Core type of a Haskell type.

A primitive's `!` parameters are forced, and an action
`World -> (utuple World a)` is made `IO a`.

**Raises** `Fail` where the two differ otherwise.

members.name: matchType
members.spec: val matchType : Core.ty * string list * Core.ty -> Core.ty list option
members.doc:
`matchType (pattern, vars, t)` is the types that `vars`, variables of
`pattern`, stand for where `pattern` is `t`.

The two are compared as `toHaskell` sees them; `NONE` where they
differ.

members.name: haskellForm
members.doc:
`haskellForm t` is the type of Core's own making `t` as Haskell sees
it: no `!`, and `IO a` for `World -> (utuple World a)`.

HS_DUMP.doc:
The abstract syntax of Haskell 98 as text, for `rhc --dump-ast` and for
the tree round trip of a test that compares trees by their text.

A node is a line: its constructor and what it holds that is not a node,
a name, a literal as written, an associativity; the nodes below it
follow, each on its line, two spaces further in. With spans, a node's
line ends with its span, `@START-STOP` in bytes of its file; without
them, two trees print the same exactly where they are equal read with
no annotations. A node's own tokens are not shown.

members.name: module
members.doc: `module {spans} m` is `m` as text, with every node's span if `spans`.

members.name: exp
members.doc: `exp {spans} e` is the expression `e` as text, as `module` writes it.

HS_EVIDENCE.doc:
The evidence records of Haskell 98's checker (the haskell98 roadmap's
D31, M13): what inference chose at each node of the renamed tree, by
node, in the manner of Rune's `Witness` (lib/compiler/elab/witness.sml),
for desugaring to Core (M15) to translate and HsLint (M16, D54) to
check: each overloaded use's dictionaries, each binder's type and the
dictionary parameters it is abstracted over, each instance's
dictionaries, and each defaulting, with what it chose from.

A type here is closed: a constructor applied to types and the type
variables of schemes, signatures and instance heads, each a rigid
variable with a name unique to the program (`HsTypes.TRigid`); a
scheme's variables are those names. A dictionary is Faxén's `dict`
judgement made explicit: a parameter in scope, an instance's dictionary
function at the types of its head's variables applied to the
dictionaries of its context ("dict inst"), or a superclass's taken from
a dictionary of its subclass ("dict super").

A node is the kind of record and the span of the node of the renamed
tree it belongs to, `KIND@FILE:START-STOP`: the name of a variable or a
constructor where it is used or bound, a literal, a negation, an
enumeration, a `do`, a pattern, an instance declaration.

members.name: dict
members.doc: A dictionary.

members.name: scheme
members.spec: type scheme = {vars : string list, ctx : HsTypes.pred list, ty : HsTypes.ty}
members.doc:
A scheme as the records hold it: its variables by name, its context
and its type, over those names.

members.name: record
members.doc: A record.

members.name: node
members.doc: `node (kind, span)` is the key of a node.

members.name: table
members.doc: A table of records by node.

members.name: empty
members.doc: `empty ()` is a new table with no record.

members.name: add
members.spec: val add : table * string * record -> unit
members.doc: `add (t, node, r)` adds the record `r` at `node`, after any there.

members.name: find
members.spec: val find : table * string -> record list
members.doc: `find (t, node)` is the records at `node`, in the order added.

members.name: all
members.spec: val all : table -> (string * record list) list
members.doc: `all t` is every record, by node, in the order of the nodes' keys.

members.name: showDict
members.doc: `showDict d` and `showRecord r` are as a dump prints them.

members.name: showRecord
members.doc: `showDict d` and `showRecord r` are as a dump prints them.

HS_FIXITY.doc:
Haskell 98's fixity resolution (the Report's 10.6, 3.4, 3.5 and 4.4.2;
the haskell98 roadmap's M12): the flat sequences of operators the parser
leaves, `HsAst.ESeq` and `HsAst.PSeq`, made into trees by the fixities of
the operators' entities, read after names (D29), so that a renamed tree
is resolved with no iteration.

A resolved sequence is a tree of sequences of two kinds only: an
operator with its operands, `[EA l, EO op, EA r]`, and a negation,
`[ENeg, EA e]`; in a pattern `[PA l, PO op, PA r]`, a negative literal
staying a `PNegLit`. What is refused, each where the source has it:

- two operators of one precedence, either of them non-associative or
  the two of different associativity (10.6), `do a == b == c` among
  them, which the Report's 9.3 gives a parse and every oracle refuses
  (R1, and R9 for `let`, as D38 pins);
- a negation where the grammar has none: after an operator of
  precedence 6 or more, `a * - b` (R10, 3.4);
- a section whose operator does not bind more loosely than its
  operand's, or as loosely on the side it associates to: `(a + b ^)`,
  `(-5 ^)`, `(+ a + b)` (3.5, R10);
- a left-hand side `p1 op p2` whose operands bind more loosely than
  its operator, `x : xs +++ ys = ...` with `+++` tighter (4.4.3);
- a negative literal as the left operand of an operator tighter than
  negation, in a pattern: `-1 :* x` (the grammar's `lpat`).

members.name: fixity
members.doc: The associativity and the precedence of an operator.

members.name: default
members.doc: An operator with no fixity declaration: `infixl 9` (4.4.2).

members.name: show
members.doc: `show f` is `f` as a declaration writes it: `infixl 6`.

members.name: resolve
members.spec:
val resolve : {fixityOf : HsAst.qname -> fixity option} -> HsAst.module
              -> HsAst.module * (HsSource.span * string) list
members.doc:
`resolve {fixityOf} m` is the renamed module `m` with every sequence
of operators resolved, and the errors of resolution in source order.

`fixityOf q` is the fixity of the operator named `q` in the renamed
tree, `NONE` for the default.

HS_IFACE.doc:
HsIface, rhc's interface of a unit (the haskell98 roadmap's M21, D44):
what a store keeps of a unit for a client, written and read back. Each
of its modules' interfaces as the renamer and the checker make them
(HsModIface). The unfoldings section is in the format from the start
and empty until M23 (D44's C). The desugaring's part, its Core among
it, is the desugaring's own text, which a client keeps beside this one:
rhc's driver keeps it as a section of its own, read only where a unit
is desugared after it.

members.name: t
members.spec: type t = {modules : HsModIface.t list, unfoldings : string list}
members.doc: A unit's interface: its modules', and the unfoldings, none yet.

members.name: Bad
members.doc: What makes bytes no interface: where, and what.

members.name: encode
members.doc:
`encode t` is `t` as bytes, which `decode` reads back: each string
once, in a table, and every place it is named a number.

A kind or a type variable linked is written as what it is linked to;
one left unsolved, which no interface's generalized types hold, raises
`Bad`.

members.name: decode
members.doc:
`decode s` is the interface `encode` wrote as `s`.

**Raises** `Bad` where `s` is not such bytes.

members.name: encodeModule
members.doc:
`encodeModule m` and `decodeModule s` are one module's interface
alone, for its tests.

members.name: decodeModule
members.doc:
`encodeModule m` and `decodeModule s` are one module's interface
alone, for its tests.

HS_INFER.doc:
Haskell 98's type checker (the haskell98 roadmap's M13, D30, D31, D32,
D33): one inference over the renamed, fixity-resolved trees of a unit,
the modules of one strongly connected group, joined, so that a binding
group or a type group may cross its modules, with what it chose
recorded by node in HsEvidence's table.

Types by first-order unification with levels; kinds by HsKinds;
classes, instances and the derived instances' contexts, by the fixpoint
10\.1 allows, in HsClasses; each overloaded use leaves a placeholder,
resolved at generalisation as a dictionary parameter, an instance's
dictionary, a superclass's, deferred outward, or defaulted. Declaration
groups by dependency of bindings alone, a signature cutting none, each
group's explicitly typed bindings apart and its implicitly typed ones
typed as one (Typing Haskell in Haskell's split in its conformant form,
R21(c)), one context for each implicit group (R21(a)),
the contexts of a group's signatures identical up to renaming (R21(b)),
a signature on a pattern binding that is not simple refused (R19), and
